facts.text: On 24 November 1978 the applicant was arrested by the police for being in possession of a firearm.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  On 24 November 1978 the applicant was arrested by the police for being in possession of a firearm. He was taken into custody at the Ankara Security Directorate and accused of having taken part in an armed attack on a bank.

facts.text: On 5 December 1978 a magistrate ordered the applicant’s provisional detention.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  On 5 December 1978 a magistrate ordered the applicant’s provisional detention.

facts.text: The public prosecutor attached to the Ankara Martial Law Court charged the applicant with being an accessory to the crime of murder and with having taken part in an armed robbery of a bank and having fired shots into a café.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  Subsequently, the public prosecutor attached to the Ankara Martial Law Court charged the applicant with being an accessory to the crime of murder and with having taken part in an armed robbery of a bank and having fired shots into a café. According to the prosecutor, the offences were committed as part of a terrorist campaign aimed at overthrowing the constitutional order, a campaign conducted by an illegal organisation, Dev‑Yol (Devrimci Yol - the Revolutionary Way).

facts.text: In its judgment of 26 September 1979 the Ankara Martial Law Court found the applicant guilty as charged and commuted the death penalty to life imprisonment.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  In its judgment of 26 September 1979 the Ankara Martial Law Court found the applicant guilty as charged. Although the applicant could have faced the death penalty for the offences at issue, the court commuted this to life imprisonment.

facts.text: The applicant and the prosecutor appealed to the Court of Cassation.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  The applicant and the prosecutor appealed to the Court of Cassation.

facts.text: On 20 August 1980 the Military Court of Cassation quashed the lower court’s judgment on the ground that the facts of the case had not been properly established.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  In its decision of 20 August 1980 the Military Court of Cassation quashed the lower court’s judgment on the ground that the facts of the case had not been properly established.

facts.text: On 28 April 1986 the applicant was released on parole.

facts.text: On 3 July 1986 the Ankara Martial Law Court partially complied with the Court of Cassation’s decision and sentenced the applicant to fifteen years imprisonment for accessory to murder and membership of an armed gang.

anchor.surface_text: 16.  In its judgment of 3 July 1986 the Ankara Martial Law Court complied partially with the Court of Cassation’s decision of 20 August 1980 and sentenced the applicant to a term of imprisonment of fifteen years on the accessory to murder charge as well as on the charge of membership of an armed gang.

facts.text: The applicant and the prosecutor lodged an appeal against the 3 July 1986 judgment; the prosecutor sought conviction for armed robbery and acquittal for accessory to murder.

anchor.surface_text: 17.  The applicant and the prosecutor lodged an appeal against the judgment. The prosecutor sought the applicant’s conviction in respect of the armed robbery charge and his acquittal in respect of the accessory to murder charge.

facts.text: On 23 December 1987 the Military Court of Cassation confirmed the applicant’s conviction on the murder charge and quashed the acquittal on the armed robbery charge.

anchor.surface_text: 18.  On 23 December 1987 the Military Court of Cassation confirmed the applicant’s conviction on the murder charge and quashed the judgment of the Ankara Martial Law Court insofar as it acquitted the applicant of the armed robbery charge.

facts.text: The public prosecutor sought rectification of the 23 December 1987 judgment to lift initial charges and categorize the charge as active membership of an armed gang.

anchor.surface_text: 19.  The public prosecutor attached to the Military Court of Cassation sought the rectification of the judgment of 23 December 1987 and requested that the initial charges be lifted and that the charge against the applicant be categorised as one of active membership of an armed gang.

facts.text: On 22 September 1988 the Military Court of Cassation quashed the applicant’s conviction for accessory to murder but found him guilty of armed robbery and remitted the case to the Ankara Martial Law Court.

anchor.surface_text: 20.  In its decision of 22 September 1988, the Military Court of Cassation quashed the applicant’s conviction for being an accessory to the crime of murder but considered that he was guilty of armed robbery. The court remitted the case file to the Ankara Martial Law Court.

facts.text: On 27 February 1990 the Ankara Martial Law Court issued a new arrest warrant against the applicant.

anchor.surface_text: 21.  On 27 February 1990 the Ankara Martial Law Court issued a new arrest warrant against the applicant.

facts.text: On 18 November 1993 the Ankara Martial Law Court sentenced the applicant to three years and two months imprisonment for membership of an armed gang and acquitted him of remaining charges.

anchor.surface_text: 22.  On 18 November 1993 the Ankara Martial Law Court sentenced the applicant to a period of imprisonment of three years and two months for membership of an armed gang and acquitted him of the remaining charges.

facts.text: By judgment dated 22 December 1993 and notified on 3 August 1994, the Military Court of Cassation declared the criminal proceedings against the applicant time-barred.

issues.text: Whether the Court has jurisdiction ratione temporis in respect of the application given the entry into force of Protocol No. 11 to the Convention

anchor.surface_text: A question arises as to the Court’s jurisdiction ratione temporis in respect of the application at issue in view of the entry into force of Protocol No. 11 to the Convention. The Court notes in this connection that on 1 November 1998, by operation of that Protocol, applications such as the instant one pending before the Commission (see paragraph 4 above) which have not been declared admissible fell to be examined by the Court in accordance with the provisions of the Protocol.

issues.text: Whether the length of the criminal proceedings was reasonable considering the complexity of the case, the applicant’s conduct and that of the competent authorities

anchor.surface_text: With reference to the principles set out in its established case-law in this area, the Court will assess the reasonableness of the impugned period in light of the complexity of the case, the applicant’s conduct and that of the competent authorities (see, among many other authorities, the above-mentioned Mitap and Müftüoğlu judgment, p. 411, § 32).

anchor.surface_text: In this connection, the applicant maintained that the domestic courts were to be faulted for their failure to process the case with due diligence as evidenced by the fact that the proceedings were punctuated by frequent, unexplained and unjustified periods of delay.
